title: Avoiding Exponentially Large Groups with Open Quantum System Technology
authors: Jihong Cai, Advith Govindarajan, Marius Junge
abstract: We propose a novel approach to state preparation by embracing the full power of open quantum systems. Instead of working with the whole unitary group in $n$ qubits, we identify a small Lie group $G$ in $(n+3)$ qubits. The dimension of its Lie algebra is $\text{poly}(n)$. Every state can be approximated starting from any fixed input state by repeatedly using partial trace and state preparation in the environment alongside group operations. Moreover, we also identify a single (open system magic) interaction Hamiltonian whose unitary group can be combined with open system quantum technology mentioned above to achieve transitivity on the space of all densities. Similarly, we show that all channels on $n$ qubits can be approximated by using a larger environment, achieving channel universality. The interesting small groups we identify are derived from Lie algebras of local Pauli strings and lead to a new landscape of cheap and expensive states, densities, and channels.
summary: This theoretical paper proposes a novel method to achieve universal state and channel control in open quantum systems by restricting the available operations to a small, polynomially-sized Lie group derived from local Pauli strings. By leveraging the environment and partial trace, the authors demonstrate that complex, global operations can be simulated efficiently, bypassing the need to control the entire unitary group.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of achieving universal state and channel preparation in open quantum systems without relying on the full, exponentially large unitary group.
main_result: They show that state and channel universality can be achieved by identifying small, polynomially-sized Lie groups derived from local Pauli strings, and by utilizing the environment to extend the available operations.
method: The approach involves characterizing the achievable set of operations (channels) using the framework of open quantum systems, specifically by analyzing the Lie algebra generated by the available unitary and dissipative operations.
model_or_system: The system consists of a primary system A (n qubits) coupled to an environment E, whose dynamics are governed by open quantum system master equations (Lindbladians). The operations are derived from combining group operations $G$ with environment interactions $V$.
key_observables: State density matrices $ho$, quantum channels $\Phi$, and the approximation error $\varepsilon$ for state/channel preparation.
important_parameters: The dimension of the generated Lie algebra, which is shown to be polynomial in $n$ rather than exponential.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the ability to approximate the required operations using a small, structured Lie group $G$ and an environment interaction $V$.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates a trade-off comparison between three models for state preparation complexity: closed system (exponential), using a small group $G$ (polynomial), and using a single interaction Hamiltonian.
paper_structure: The paper develops the mathematical framework for open system operations, defines state and channel transitivity, and then proves theorems establishing that polynomial resources (small Lie groups) can achieve universality, contrasting this with the exponential complexity of the full unitary group.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete, resource-efficient pathways for quantum control, showing that structured local interactions can simulate the power of global, complex gates, which is crucial for designing practical quantum hardware protocols.
